html:
Tilián is the name the map gives to a small people of the Quebrada de Humahuaca, the long valley of Jujuy in north-western Argentina. Spanish records list several local groups in this valley, among them the Tilcaras, Purmamarcas and Humahuacas, often grouped together as the Omaguaca.

Little is known about the Tilián as a separate group. The valley people farmed maize on terraces, herded llamas and built hilltop forts. From the 1400s the Inca Empire ruled the valley, and after the Spanish conquest it became a road between Potosí and the south. Their neighbours included the Kolla and Atacameño of the high puna.
